messages:
shreya: Ran the long-context benchmark (longload-2k4) overnight on staging-rt2. Not great — steady memory growth ~12MB/hr, baseline used to be ~0.5MB/hr. Paging/eviction rate jumps after ~3h :thinking_face:

matt: Yikes. Any repro steps or command you used?

shreya: Command + short results:
```
./bench --workload long-context --seq=2048 --clients=8 --duration=6h \\  --kv-cache=on --batch=dynamic --seed=42

Summary (start -> end):
  p50: 82ms -> 90ms
  p95: 210ms -> 260ms
  tokens/s: 13.1k -> 11.8k
  mem_gb: 6.1 -> 12.2
  kv_evictions: 1.2k -> 9.8k
  page_faults/min: 2 -> 18
```

liam: Can you paste the jemalloc stats / heap profile at the 4h mark? If fragmentation is the culprit we should see high retained by small extents.

shreya: Pasted the relevant snippet from the heap dump at 4:03AM:
```
heap_summary:
  total_allocs: 14.8M
  retained: 11.9GB
  fragment_ratio: 1.28
  tracked_objects:
    kv_extent: 12.3M (dominant)
    small_allocs(<4KB): 3.1M
  largest_free_chunk: 1.2MB
  arena_count: 8
```

shreya: Also saw logs with repeated small frees/allocs for kv fragments, and compaction only triggers rarely.

matt: This smells like a reuse-path regression: earlier we coalesced extents more aggressively on retire, but last patch to rotation heuristics reduced coalescing to avoid stalls. Might be the performance patch tradeoff backfiring for long-live contexts.

liam: Agreed. Two hypotheses: (1) small-fragment churn due to slab rotation change; (2) eviction policy causing repeated re-alloc/free of similar sized extents (thrashing). We should add counters for allocs/frees by bucket size and measure coalesces per minute.

eva: Can we reproduce with a smaller local loop? I can run a deterministic interleaved workload that forces reuse patterns — easier to iterate. I can also add a jemalloc config to force aggressive coalescing and see impact.

shreya: I already ran a quick local with MALLOC_CONF: "oversize_threshold:1,dirty_decay_ms:-1,muzzy_decay_ms:-1" and mem growth flattened, eviction count halved. So allocator config affects it. But we can't rely on that in prod; we need a runtime-level fix or a guardrail in the kvcache.

matt: Proposed action items:
  - add CI long-context smoke test (2h) that fails if mem growth > 1MB/hr or kv_evictions increase > 2x baseline
  - add telemetry counters: allocs_by_bucket, coalesces/min, compaction_invocations/min
  - reproduce locally with interleaved-prefix workload (eva)
  - create a perf experiment that toggles slab rotation/coalesce thresholds (liam)

liam: I'll own the perf experiment. Plan: run 3x 6h jobs with these params: baseline, rotation-old (pre-change), rotation-new. Measure retained, frag, p95, evictions. I'll post results in this thread.

eva: I'll wire a deterministic workload harness called "longcontext-reuse-interop" that simulates 4 clients, each appending 2k tokens and then jumping back to reused prefixes at 30% probability. Hook it into the bench infra and add a label for CI.

shreya: For the CI test, suggest thresholds and sampling cadence:
  - run 2h on a smaller instance (same heap/arena config)
  - sample mem_gb every 5m, require slope < 1 MB/hr projected
  - check eviction rate parity +/- 25% vs baseline
  - fail if fragmentation_ratio > 1.15 at end

matt: Those look reasonable. Might want a relaxed threshold for p95 (avoid false positives) but strict for mem growth. Also add an automatic link to the heap snapshot if CI fails.

perf-bot: experiment queued: perf/kv/rotation-experiment-2151234578 (6h). Results will post when done.

shreya: Quick patch idea: on retire of small extents, attempt coalesce with neighbor up to X retries within background worker to avoid blocking hot path. If coalesce fails keep as-is. That should reduce fragmentation without regressing latency. Need to bench.

liam: That sounds good — please make it behind a flag. We'll compare with rotation-old/new. Also add a microbenchmark for coalesce success rate.

eva: I'll add the CI job and the deterministic workload today. Also adding log markers at compaction start/end so we can correlate with heap snaps.

matt: OK. Owners: liam (perf experiment + telemetry), eva (harness + CI job), shreya (heap analysis + proposed patch PR). ETA: EOD for initial experiments?

liam: EOD for experiment triage, full runs ~24h.

shreya: Thanks all. If anyone sees a spike in pager faults on staging-rt2, please tag me. :eyes:

matt: Thanks — ping when you have the perf-bot results. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: perf/kv/rotation-experiment-2151234578 completed: baseline vs rotation-old vs rotation-new comparative report uploaded: https://perf.internal/2151234578

shreya: Got the report. Initial glance: rotation-old has lowest fragmentation (frag_ratio 1.12) and stable mem; rotation-new matches latency improvements but frag_ratio 1.28 after 6h. Uploading annotated diffs shortly.

matt: Nice. Looks like we should revert the aggressive change or gate it behind workload heuristics. We'll discuss in next runtime sync.

liam: Filed perf task: RUNTIME-6292 (investigate kvcache coalesce heuristics).

eva: CI job added: longcontext-memory-stability-2h, will be green on PR once harness merged.

shreya: Marking follow-ups done in a doc: https://docs.internal/kv-longcontext-regressions (will add heap diffs).

matt: Great thread. Short-term: add CI guardrail + telemetry. Medium-term: coalesce fix behind flag + perf comparison.

liam: :+1:

eva: :thumbsup:

shreya: Closing this thread for now — will repost when I have the PR and annotated heap diffs.
